# Fleet GitRepo — OpenChoreo.
#
# This is the Fleet `GitRepo` CUSTOM RESOURCE (gitrepos.fleet.cattle.io), not a
# git repository: it points Fleet at the existing lab-fleet repo and tells it
# which paths to render. It lives on the RANCHER CONTROLLER
# (192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`), so it is not part of any bundle here.
#
#   kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openchoreo.yaml
#
# ─── This one breaks the lab-<namespace> convention, deliberately ────────────
# Every other GitRepo here owns exactly one namespace. OpenChoreo spans SEVEN
# (openchoreo-control-plane, -data-plane, -workflow-plane, -observability-plane,
# thunder, openbao, external-secrets) and they are not independently useful: a
# data plane with no control plane is nothing, and the planes register with
# each other over mTLS. Splitting them into seven GitRepos would give seven
# knobs that must always be turned together, and would scatter one product's
# rollout across seven files.
#
# So this is one GitRepo per PRODUCT, staged by `spec.paths` — the same
# mechanism `lab-ai` uses, for the same reason.
#
# ─── ✅ ROLLOUT COMPLETE 2026-07-30 — this file now matches the live GitRepo ──
# `paths` below holds ALL TWENTY paths, in install order, and is what is
# actually running on the cluster. Re-applying this file is now SAFE and is
# the correct way to reconcile the GitRepo.
#

# Fleet GitRepos — one per namespace

These are Fleet **`GitRepo` custom resources** (`gitrepos.fleet.cattle.io`), not
git repositories. Each one points Fleet at the existing `lab-fleet` repo and
lists which paths to render. They live on the **Rancher controller**
(192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`) — not on sdf1 — so they are not part
of any bundle in this repo. Kept here as the versioned source of record.

    kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-node-red.yaml

Applying any file here is a **single** adoption step, and idempotent once adopted —
no file holds more than one unadopted path (see the rule below). The exception is
`lab-ai`, which has **no file at all** and is staged by hand — see below.

> **🔴 Corrections learned by breaking things on 2026-07-30. Read these
> before adopting anything.**
>
> **1. Removing a path does NOT roll back — it uninstalls.** For a bundle whose
> Helm release Fleet has taken ownership of, deleting the path runs the
> equivalent of `helm uninstall`. This deleted karakeep's StatefulSets,
> Deployment, Service, Ingress and one PVC. Use `spec.paused: true` to stop Fleet
> acting, and fix forward. Only `spec.paths` removal on a bundle that never
> reached ownership is safe.
>
> **2. A nested path is not a staging gate.** Fleet deploys `<path>/<child>` as
> soon as `<path>` is adopted, whether or not the child is in `spec.paths`.
> Gating only works between SIBLING paths (`01-networking` and
> `01-networking/pools`). The "then patch in the second path" note that used to
> appear on `lab-buzz`, `lab-lab-memory` and `lab-cert-manager` was wrong and has
> been corrected.
>
> **3. `kubectl diff` clean does not predict Fleet.** Fleet applies server-side
> and needs field *ownership*. Pre-flight any pre-existing Helm release with
> `kubectl apply --server-side --dry-run=server`, which surfaces the
> field-manager conflicts `kubectl diff` normalises away.
>
> **4. When adopting a parent path, remove the explicit child path in the SAME
> patch.** With both `04-ollama/ollama-exporter` and `04-ollama` in
> `spec.paths`, the gitjob wrote the exporter bundle twice in one pass and
> died fatal on its own conflict ("object has been modified") — three
> identical failures, unblocked only by dropping the child entry. This is
> safe against correction 1: the parent scan still defines the bundle under
> the identical name, so nothing uninstalls. A `.fleetignore` in the parent
> does NOT prevent nested-bundle discovery — it filters bundle content only —
> so it cannot be used to keep the pair.
>
> Details and evidence are in `FLEET-WIRING.md`.

## Convention: `lab-<namespace>`

One GitRepo per Kubernetes namespace, so each namespace's workloads can be
adopted, rolled back, or paused independently of every other.

|---|---|---|---|

| `lab-emby` | `emby` | `11-emby` | low |
| `lab-resilio` | `resilio` | `13-resilio` | low |
| `lab-ash4d-origin` | `ash4d-origin` | `16-ash4d-origin` | low |

Two different knobs here, and the repo's docs already warn about picking the wrong one.

## Don't remove paths

`22-openchoreo/README.md:370` and `gitrepos/README.md:19` both say it: removing a path from `spec.paths` is a `helm uninstall`, not a pause. For `22-openchoreo/control-plane` that takes 36 CRDs and every Project/Component/Workload with them.

## Easiest = pause the GitRepo

```bash
kubectl --context rancher patch gitrepo lab-openchoreo -n fleet-default \
  --type merge -p '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'
```

One field, fully reversible, and it's the documented mechanism. **But it only stops Fleet from acting — every pod keeps running.** Right now that's 24 Deployments + 4 StatefulSets across 7 namespaces, roughly 6 GiB by the footprint table at `22-openchoreo/README.md:293`.

## If the point is reclaiming the node

Pause first, then scale to zero:

```bash
for ns in openchoreo-control-plane openchoreo-data-plane openchoreo-workflow-plane \
          openchoreo-observability-plane thunder openbao external-secrets; do
  kubectl --context sdf1 -n $ns scale deploy,sts --all --replicas=0
done
```

Everything is currently at 1 replica, so `--replicas=1` restores it exactly. `correctDrift` is off on this GitRepo, so nothing fights you; pausing just makes it deterministic against a future commit re-rendering a bundle.

Coming back:

```bash
for ns in external-secrets openbao thunder openchoreo-control-plane \
          openchoreo-data-plane openchoreo-workflow-plane openchoreo-observability-plane; do
  kubectl --context sdf1 -n $ns scale deploy,sts --all --replicas=1
done
kubectl --context rancher patch gitrepo lab-openchoreo -n fleet-default \
  --type merge -p '{"spec":{"paused":false}}'
```

Three things worth knowing before you do it:

- **OpenBao is dev mode** — in-memory, reseeds from its `fleet.yaml` fixtures on start. Seeded secrets come back identical; anything you created through the OpenChoreo UI does not.
- **Thunder and Backstage use in-pod SQLite** — hand-added users/OIDC clients are lost, fixtures are recreated by the bootstrap Job.
- **OpenSearch, Prometheus and the registry are on Longhorn PVCs** — scaling to 0 keeps the data; the PVCs stay bound and keep occupying Longhorn either way.

I checked that ESO is only serving OpenChoreo (3 ExternalSecrets, all in openchoreo namespaces), so shutting it down doesn't touch anything else in the fleet.

Want me to add a "Suspending" section to `22-openchoreo/README.md` with these commands? It sits naturally next to the Rollback section, and the ordering nuances are easy to lose.

content.text:
Short answer: no — but the reason matters, because it's a property of your config, not of Fleet's defaults.

## Why it won't

I confirmed on the live BundleDeployments that `correctDrift` is unset:

```
$ kubectl --context rancher get bundledeployment lab-openchoreo-22-openchoreo-control-plane \
    -n cluster-fleet-default-c-nnzn9-eaf6ebdbb298 -o jsonpath='{.spec.options.correctDrift}'
null
```

That matches `correctDrift.enabled: false` in `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openchoreo.yaml:113`. The agent does run a drift reconciler (`DRIFT_RECONCILER_WORKERS=50` on `fleet-agent`), but with correction off it only *detects and reports* — your bundles flip to `Modified` and sit there. `FLEET-WIRING.md:463` is that exact shape observed on this cluster: a field Fleet re-renders, never sees land, and "reports `Modified` forever with no path to convergence."

So expect all 20 bundles to go `Modified` after a scale-down. That's cosmetic, not Fleet fighting you.

## What *would* turn it back on

Not the drift loop — a **redeploy**. Fleet re-runs the chart (restoring `replicas: 1`) when the deploymentID changes, which means:

- any commit touching `22-openchoreo/**` — and `pollingInterval: 60s` means within a minute
- editing the GitRepo itself (paths, values, even adding an unrelated field)
- Rancher UI "Force Update", or a `fleet.cattle.io/redeploy` annotation

`spec.paused: true` is precisely what closes off that first path, which is why I'd pause *before* scaling rather than treating it as optional. Without the pause, scale-to-0 holds only until the next time you touch this repo.

## Two things that aren't Fleet

- **No HPAs** anywhere on sdf1 — I checked. Nothing auto-scales back.
- **OpenChoreo's own controllers.** The `controller-manager` pods in the control and observability planes are themselves in the scale-down set, so there's a brief window where a controller is still up while its peers are going to zero. Not a real risk given nothing CR-driven is deployed, but re-run the loop and confirm everything reads `0/0` rather than assuming one pass took.

## Cheap way to prove it before committing

```bash
kubectl --context sdf1 -n openchoreo-observability-plane scale deploy observer --replicas=0
```

Leave it 20 minutes (past the 15m `CHECKIN_INTERVAL`). If it's still `0/0` and the bundle reads `Modified`, the behavior is confirmed and you can run the full loop. I've verified the config, not the outcome — this closes that gap for the cost of one pod.

## One correction to what I told you

I said nothing would turn it back on. That was right about **Fleet** — `observer` sat at `0/0` for seven hours untouched, and every Deployment I scaled stayed scaled. But it wasn't the whole answer: `prometheus-openchoreo-observability` and `alertmanager-openchoreo-observability` aren't Fleet-driven leaf objects. They're owned by `Prometheus`/`Alertmanager` CRs reconciled by `rancher-monitoring-operator` in `cattle-monitoring-system` — a controller outside this GitRepo entirely, still running. It reset the StatefulSet replicas within seconds, which is why you saw `prometheus-...-0` come back as `PodInitializing`.

The fix was to scale the CRs rather than the StatefulSets. Worth internalizing as the general rule: **`kubectl scale` on an operator-owned workload is a no-op with extra steps** — check `ownerReferences` first.

Also: `error: no objects passed to scale` on namespaces with no StatefulSet is what made the loop exit 1. Probably what bit your original run too, if the combined `deploy,sts` form aborted the whole call.

## Restore is now four steps, not one

```bash
for ns in openchoreo-control-plane openchoreo-data-plane openchoreo-workflow-plane \
          openchoreo-observability-plane thunder openbao external-secrets; do
  kubectl --context sdf1 -n "$ns" scale deploy --all --replicas=1
  kubectl --context sdf1 -n "$ns" scale sts    --all --replicas=1
done
kubectl --context sdf1 -n openchoreo-observability-plane patch prometheus   openchoreo-observability --type merge -p '{"spec":{"replicas":1}}'
kubectl --context sdf1 -n openchoreo-observability-plane patch alertmanager openchoreo-observability --type merge -p '{"spec":{"replicas":1}}'
kubectl --context sdf1 -n openchoreo-observability-plane patch ds fluent-bit --type merge -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":null}}}}'
kubectl --context rancher patch gitrepo lab-openchoreo -n fleet-default --type merge -p '{"spec":{"paused":false}}'
```

I also parked the `fluent-bit` DaemonSet with an unsatisfiable `nodeSelector` (it has no `ownerReferences`, so it's chart-managed and the patch will stick) — that's the third line above, reverting it.

Unbound state to be aware of: the OpenSearch, Prometheus and registry PVCs are still bound and still counted against Longhorn's scheduled capacity, which `FLEET-WIRING.md:230` notes was 759 of 764 GiB. Suspending didn't give any of that back.

This is exactly the kind of procedure that's painful to reconstruct in two months, and the operator-owned CR trap is a genuinely non-obvious footgun. Want me to write it up as a "Suspending" section in `22-openchoreo/README.md` next to Rollback, plus a watch-out in `FLEET-WIRING.md`?

Restore first: **all 20 bundles `ready=1`, zero `modified`**, node back to 73%, Fleet unpaused and reconciling. That's fully closed out.

Now correctDrift. I checked the two things that would make this dangerous, and the picture is better than your docs imply:

**Zero bundles report `Modified` across all 12 live GitRepos.** There is no active drift anywhere on this cluster right now — so turning correction on has nothing to fight today.

**The cert-manager landmine is already closed.** `FLEET-WIRING.md:469` warns those DNS-01 flags live only on the running Deployment, which would have made correctDrift a delayed cluster-wide cert outage. But `15-cert-manager/values.yaml:27-29` now carries them, and I confirmed they match the live args exactly. That risk is retired.

The `FLEET-WIRING.md:170` warning says "leave it disabled **at first**" — that was adoption-time advice, and adoption is done. Two things still give me pause:

1. **openchoreo.** `lab-openchoreo.yaml:107` argues against it specifically, because OpenChoreo's controllers write to objects in those namespaces during normal operation. Today's prometheus-operator discovery is a live example of foreign controllers in that namespace. Its zero-drift reading is also weak evidence — the stack is 8 hours old and idle, with no Projects or Components deployed. Controller writes would show up once it's actually used.
2. **`lab-ai` has no GitRepo file** — it's the hand-staged one. Enabling it means a live patch with nothing in git recording it, which breaks the "versioned source of record" property the other 11 have.

The timing is my real hesitation: if correctDrift does start fighting a controller, the failure mode is a hot reconcile loop, and you won't see it until morning.

# Fleet GitRepo — OpenChoreo.
#
# This is the Fleet `GitRepo` CUSTOM RESOURCE (gitrepos.fleet.cattle.io), not a
# git repository: it points Fleet at the existing lab-fleet repo and tells it
# which paths to render. It lives on the RANCHER CONTROLLER
# (192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`), so it is not part of any bundle here.
#
#   kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openchoreo.yaml
#
# ─── This one breaks the lab-<namespace> convention, deliberately ────────────
# Every other GitRepo here owns exactly one namespace. OpenChoreo spans SEVEN
# (openchoreo-control-plane, -data-plane, -workflow-plane, -observability-plane,
# thunder, openbao, external-secrets) and they are not independently useful: a
# data plane with no control plane is nothing, and the planes register with
# each other over mTLS. Splitting them into seven GitRepos would give seven
# knobs that must always be turned together, and would scatter one product's
# rollout across seven files.
#
# So this is one GitRepo per PRODUCT, staged by `spec.paths` — the same
# mechanism `lab-ai` uses, for the same reason.
#
# ─── ✅ ROLLOUT COMPLETE 2026-07-30 — this file now matches the live GitRepo ──
# `paths` below holds ALL TWENTY paths, in install order, and is what is
# actually running on the cluster. Re-applying this file is now SAFE and is
# the correct way to reconcile the GitRepo.
#
# It was not safe during the staged rollout. Until 2026-07-30 this file held
# path 1 only while the live GitRepo was widened by hand, so `kubectl apply -f`
# would have narrowed `spec.paths` back to a single entry. FLEET-WIRING.md
# records that exact mistake on lab-lab-memory, where re-applying a GitRepo
# file to add `pollingInterval` silently reverted a hand-narrowed `spec.paths`
# and restarted a failing retry loop. Keep this list in sync with the live
# resource from here on, and the trap stays closed.
#
# Narrowing is still not a rollback. For `22-openchoreo/control-plane` in
# particular, removing the path uninstalls the release and takes 36 CRDs and
# every OpenChoreo object in the cluster with it. Use `spec.paused: true`.
#
# ─── Fresh install, not an adoption ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Unlike almost everything else in this repo, none of these paths adopts an
# existing release — nothing OpenChoreo-related was on the cluster beforehand.
# So the SSA field-ownership pre-flight in FLEET-WIRING.md does not apply here:
# there is no `helm` field manager to hand over from. What replaces it is
# ordering and prerequisites, which are strict. Read 22-openchoreo/README.md
# before the first apply — in particular the cluster-gateway CA bootstrap,
# which is the one step Fleet cannot do.
apiVersion: fleet.cattle.io/v1alpha1
kind: GitRepo
metadata:
  name: lab-openchoreo
  namespace: fleet-default
spec:
  repo: https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet
  branch: main
  # Explicit polling interval. Fleet's default is 15s, but this cluster's
  # gitjob runs with `gitjob.syncPeriod: 2h` (a Rancher fleet-chart value), and
  # on 2026-07-30 four GitRepos went dormant for 28+ minutes after a single
  # transient `context deadline exceeded` against github.com -- they only
  # recovered when an external write forced a reconcile. Stating the interval
  # here bounds how stale a repo can get and makes the intent reviewable in git
  # rather than depending on a controller-wide default. See FLEET-WIRING.md.
  pollingInterval: 60s
  paths:
    # All twenty, in install order — matches the live GitRepo as of 2026-07-30.
    # NOTE `22-openchoreo` itself must NEVER appear in this list: a nested
    # fleet.yaml deploys as soon as its parent path is adopted, so adding the

Same pod objects, never recreated, and a broken pip install inside the image. It's been crashlooping for two weeks — enabling drift correction just made Fleet surface it in the GitRepo status where it had been invisible before. Arguably a small win.

**correctDrift is on for all 12 live GitRepos**, propagated to all 36 BundleDeployments (the two `fleet-agent-*` ones are Fleet's own and stay off). Every other bundle is clean — no drift, no errors, no reconcile loops.

Three things I decided along the way that you should know about:

- **The 4 un-adopted GitRepo files stay `false`** — `cattle-monitoring-system`, `longhorn-system`, `metallb-system`, `nvidia-device-plugin`. They aren't deployed, and correctDrift enabled *at adoption time* is precisely the hazard the original comment warns about. Turning it on for them would arm a trap for whoever adopts them next.
- **`lab-ai` was patched live**, since it has no file. It's now the one GitRepo whose correctDrift setting exists nowhere in git.
- **`lab-openchoreo.yaml` got a real comment**, not a rewrite — it records that this was a deliberate override, that the controller-vs-Fleet concern is untested rather than retired, that zero-drift on an idle 8-hour-old stack is weak evidence, and that it's the first thing to flip back if something flaps. It also notes today's `rancher-monitoring-operator` finding.

# Handoff

Capture everything a fresh session needs to continue this work, so the current
session can be ended without losing ground.

**Why this exists.** Every turn re-reads the entire accumulated prefix, so cost
per turn climbs with session length — measured at ~26K cache-read tokens per
turn in short sessions versus ~109K past 100 turns. Ending a long session at a
clean boundary and restarting with a handoff is the largest available
efficiency lever. The handoff is what makes ending cheap.

## Where to write it

```
~/.claude/handoffs/<cwd-with-slashes-as-dashes>.md
```

For example, `/Users/rashford/Developer/kitsune` →
`~/.claude/handoffs/-Users-rashford-Developer-kitsune.md`

Overwrite any existing file for this directory — the newest handoff wins. The
`SessionStart` hook loads it automatically in the next session, so **do not**
paste the contents back into chat.

## What to write

Aim for something a competent stranger could act on. Be concrete: real paths,
real command names, real decisions. Skip anything reconstructible from the repo
or from `git log` — those are already available to the next session.

```markdown
# Handoff — <one-line description of the work>
Written: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> · Session: <turns> turns

## Where things stand
Two or three sentences. What was being worked on and what state it is in
right now — not a history of the session.

## Decisions made (and why)
Only decisions that would otherwise be re-litigated. Include the reasoning,
because the reasoning is the part that gets lost.

## Files touched
- `path/to/file` — what changed and why

## What's verified vs assumed
Explicit. If tests ran, say so and give the result. If something was assumed
and never checked, say that too — this is the section that prevents the next
session from building on sand.

## Next step
The single next action, stated concretely. Then anything queued behind it.

## Open questions
Things the user needs to decide, or that were left unresolved.
```

## Procedure

1. **Write the file.** Use the path convention above. Do not ask where to put it.
2. **Confirm briefly** — one line naming the file and the next step it records.
3. **Tell the user to `/clear`** (or start a new session). Do not run `/clear`
   yourself; it is theirs to trigger.

## Notes

- Leave out anything sensitive — the handoff is plain text on disk.
- Handoffs older than 14 days are ignored by the loader.
- To skip loading a handoff for one session, start with `HANDOFF_DISABLE=1`.
- If the user asks for a handoff without wanting to stop, write it anyway and
  skip the `/clear` suggestion.

# Handoff — OpenChoreo v1.2.1 (`22-openchoreo`) staged Fleet rollout, 8 of 20 paths live
Written: 2026-07-30 20:10 · Session: ~35 turns

## Where things stand

OpenChoreo's **control plane is deployed, healthy and serving over HTTPS** —
`https://openchoreo.ash4d.com` returns 200 (Backstage portal),
`https://api.openchoreo.ash4d.com/health` returns 200, real Let's Encrypt cert
valid to 2026-10-28. Fleet GitRepo `lab-openchoreo` is at **8/8 bundles ready**
with 8 of 20 paths enabled. The bundle is merged to `main` (PR #16, commit
`4604268`); local repo on `main`, tree clean.

The remaining 12 paths (Thunder, data / workflow / observability planes,
registration) are **not enabled**. `thunder.ash4d.com` currently 404s — correct
and expected, since Thunder is path 9 and nothing claims that hostname yet.

`22-openchoreo/README.md` is the authoritative runbook (install order,
prerequisites, bootstrap, rollback). Don't re-derive from this handoff what
that file already says.

## Decisions made (and why)

- **Traefik fronts kgateway; the Gateways are ClusterIP.** All `ash4d.com` DNS
  points at Traefik (192.168.7.150) and MetalLB's `lan-pool` had only 5 free
  addresses. A class-wide `GatewayParameters` (`22-openchoreo/kgateway-params/`)
  forces every kgateway Gateway Service to ClusterIP, wired via
  `gatewayClassParametersRefs` in `kgateway/values.yaml`. Biggest deviation from
  upstream and the reason several values files disagree with its reference install.
- **Do NOT install Gateway API CRDs.** v1.5.1 standard channel is already on the
  cluster, owned by the k3s `traefik-crd` release with
  `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`. Upstream's installer applies exactly that
  version; doing so would aim Fleet at k3s's own cluster-scoped objects.
- **The metrics module must not run its own prometheus-operator or CRDs.**
  `rancher-monitoring` (operator v0.87.1, watches all namespaces) already owns
  them. `observability-metrics/values.yaml` sets
  `kube-prometheus-stack.crds.enabled: false` and
  `prometheusOperator.enabled: false`, letting Rancher's operator reconcile
  OpenChoreo's `Prometheus`/`Alertmanager`. Leaves a v0.87.1-CRD / v0.88.1-chart
  skew — why that path is last and explicitly droppable.
- **Workloads live at `*.apps.openchoreo.ash4d.com`**, not the originally planned
  `*.openchoreoapis.ash4d.com`. The user's `*.openchoreo.ash4d.com` wildcard
  resolves at arbitrary depth, so no extra DNS record is needed. The nested
  `apps.` label stops a component named `api` or `observer` from shadowing the
  control plane's own hostnames.
- **Registration is declarative, not a bootstrap step.** Upstream shells out for
  each plane's agent CA and inlines PEM. The v1.2.1 CRDs also accept
  `clientCA.secretKeyRef` with a cross-namespace `namespace`, so
  `22-openchoreo/registration/` references each plane's `cluster-agent-tls`
  Secret instead.
- **OpenBao runs in dev mode (in-memory), deliberately.** File storage persists
  but seals on every restart with no auto-unseal, which unattended means the
  portal silently losing credentials. Cost: secrets created through the
  OpenChoreo UI do not survive a restart.
- **`thunder/values.yaml` and `openbao/values.yaml` commit credential values** —
  OpenChoreo's *published* upstream fixtures. Bounded exception to the repo's
  no-secrets rule; each must byte-match across an OIDC handshake and Thunder's
  half lives in a 34 KB bootstrap script. All hostnames resolve to a LAN
  address. Rotation table in `22-openchoreo/README.md`.

## Files touched

All committed to `main` via PR #16. Nothing uncommitted.

- `22-openchoreo/` — 20 Fleet paths (13 pinned Helm charts + 7 raw) + `README.md`.
- `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openchoreo.yaml` — the GitRepo. **Holds stage 1
  only.** Re-applying it after widening resets `spec.paths` back to one entry.
- `14-cluster-mgmt/FLEET-WIRING.md` — new section: platform-scale bundle, the k3s
  CRD-ownership finding, the monitoring collision, two-default-StorageClass gotcha.
- `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/README.md`, `README.md` — index/table updates.

## What's verified vs assumed

**Verified on the live cluster:**
- Paths 1–8 deployed; `lab-openchoreo` 8/8 ready; 7/7 control-plane pods `1/1`.
- ClusterSecretStore `default` Ready=True (ESO→OpenBao auth and postStart seeding
  both work). `backstage-secrets` ExternalSecret synced.
- authz bootstrap Job succeeded: 11 ClusterAuthzRoles + 10 bindings exist.
- `openchoreo-ash4d-tls` issued by Let's Encrypt; portal + API return HTTP 200.
- GatewayClass `kgateway` Accepted=True; Gateways are ClusterIP as intended.

**Verified pre-deploy (rendering only):** all 13 charts `helm template` clean
against pinned versions with these values; the 4 hand-written CRs validate
against real v1.2.1 / kgateway v2.3.1 CRD JSON schemas.

**Known gap in that pre-flight:** rendering used `--no-hooks`, which hid the
control-plane chart's post-install hook Job (`openchoreo-authz-bootstrap`). It
failed its first attempts because it runs before `controller-manager`'s
admission webhook has endpoints, then self-healed on retry. **Expect the same
race on the remaining plane charts** — a Fleet "context deadline exceeded" on
first install is not necessarily fatal; check whether the Job retries before
intervening.

**Assumed, never verified:**
- The kgateway-provisioned Service is named `gateway-default` in the data-plane
  and observability-plane namespaces (confirmed only in the control plane). Both
  `data-plane-extras/ingress.yaml` and `observability-extras/ingress.yaml`
  hardcode that name.
- `/etc/machine-id` is non-empty on sdf1 (needed by fluent-bit in
  `observability-logs`). Never checked — run `cat /etc/machine-id` on the node.
- The v0.87.1 / v0.88.1 prometheus-operator skew is benign.

**Resolved red herring — do not re-investigate.** The DNS-01 challenge appeared
stuck ~40 min with TXT records present in Cloudflare but returning NXDOMAIN from
Cloudflare's own authoritative NS. Pure Cloudflare publishing lag; resolved
itself. The API token is fine — `/user/tokens/verify` returns "Invalid API Token"
for zone-scoped tokens while zone/DNS-record calls succeed.

## Next step

Enable **path 9, Thunder** (the OIDC provider — nothing in the portal can
authenticate without it), then confirm `https://thunder.ash4d.com` stops 404ing.
Read the live paths, append one entry, patch back the full list, wait for 9/9:

```bash
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get gitrepo lab-openchoreo -o jsonpath='{.spec.paths}'
# append "22-openchoreo/thunder" to that list, then:
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo lab-openchoreo --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"paths":[ <full list including the new entry> ]}}'
```

Queued behind it, in order (detail in `22-openchoreo/README.md`):

10. `data-plane` → 11. `data-plane-extras` → 12. `workflow-registry` →
13. `workflow-plane` → 14. `observability-extras` → 15. `observability-plane` →
16. `observability-logs` → 17. `observability-traces` →
18. `observability-events` → 19. `observability-metrics` → 20. `registration`

**Before paths 10, 13 and 15**, run the one manual bootstrap step — copy the
control plane's cluster-gateway CA into the three plane namespaces. Exact command
is in `22-openchoreo/README.md` under "Bootstrap: propagating the cluster-gateway
CA". Skipping it leaves each plane's `cluster-agent` pod in `ContainerCreating`
with a missing-ConfigMap event and nothing in the logs pointing at the cause.

Enable paths 16–19 **one at a time**, checking `kubectl top node` between each.
The node was at 74% memory (48/64 GiB) before any of this; OpenSearch alone is
~2 GiB. If it gets tight, drop `observability-metrics` first, then
`observability-traces`.

## Open questions

- **Workflow templates.** Builds have no template to run — upstream's four samples
  were deliberately excluded (two hardcode a k3d registry). Either apply the
  non-k3d pair by hand or write templates targeting `workflow-registry`. Builds
  do not work end-to-end until this is done.
- **Harbor vs the throwaway registry.** `workflow-registry` deploys a small
  unauthenticated `registry:2`. The cluster already runs Harbor at
  `registry.ash4d.com`, the better long-term target — but Harbor is outside
  lab-fleet and pointing builds at it changes retention behaviour for a registry
  the `ai` namespace depends on. Deferred, not decided.
- **Two default StorageClasses.** `local-path` and `longhorn` are both marked
  `is-default-class: true`. Every PVC in `22-openchoreo` names `longhorn`
  explicitly to work around it. Worth fixing cluster-wide, separately.
- **Rotate the fixture credentials** before anything is exposed beyond the LAN.
  Table in `22-openchoreo/README.md`. The OpenSearch password is write-once — it
  seeds the security index on first start only.
- **`correctDrift` stays off.** OpenChoreo's controllers write to objects in these
  namespaces as normal operation; enabling it risks Fleet fighting them.
